value.rationale: The infinite book-graph family is a natural minimal redundant network with two edge-price classes and an adversarial single-link-loss design problem. The exact, globally unique optimizer exhibits a saturated outage-balancing regime, an interior budget-sensitive regime, and backup-edge deletion at a second sharp threshold. The robust deletion price is strictly higher than the nominal D-optimal threshold, yielding a concrete design effect; this is more than a single numerical instance or a restatement of determinant concavity.
